title: How Farza restarted after shutting down Buildspace: daily shots, collaborators, HeyClicky
summary: Farza explains why he shut down Buildspace instead of selling it, the 6 months of doing nothing that followed, and how he rebuilt momentum by shipping something every week. Covers how he picks collaborators and hires, how HeyClicky grew out of a throwaway side project, and how he thinks about money and happiness.

principles.text: Give a nagging doubt 6 to 12 months before shutting a company down.
principles.quote: you can't just shut down four years of work in like a couple of days. Like it makes no sense. And so I was like, let me give this let me give this like at least a year, like 6 to 12 months

principles.text: A disengaged founder can't fake it; a good team sees through you immediately.
principles.quote: it's even harder to run to fake running a company. Like you can't just like pretend like you're in it cuz then the people around you if you hire a good team like they're going to see through you immediately.

principles.text: When winding down, put real effort into placing your team; this was his biggest regret.
principles.quote: put in a ton more effort to make sure everyone gets placed in the right place after versus like everyone just kind of like having to like fend for themselves in a way.

principles.text: Rebuild momentum by taking many cheap shots: ship something weekly and show at least one person.
principles.quote: My only goal every single week was basically I have to make something and I have to just at least show one person.

principles.text: Pick collaborators first for how much you enjoy talking to them, then for real skill.
principles.quote: I just enjoy having a conversation with them. ... That's like 95%. ... They actually have to be like really good at whatever they do.

principles.text: Trial candidates for up to three months before hiring to see how you collaborate.
principles.quote: I will then bring people out hopefully two to three months and work with months. ... Forget three months with everybody before hiring them because then you get a much better sense of then how you collaborate
